Honesty statement. CVSS scores are computed from the CVSS v3.1 formula (work/analysis/cvss.py), using AV:P (no network exists in this challenge) and S:U, and crediting impact only where a simulation demonstrates it. No physical board was available, so exploits are shown in cycle-accurate RTL simulation and the design is synthesized for the UP5K; board bring-up steps are documented. Claims not backed by a run are marked as such.
Contents: 1. Reverse-engineering 2. The cipher 3. AI pipeline 4. Trojans 5. CVSS 6. Key recovery 7. Resources 8. Reproduce

1. Bitstream reverse-engineering

The provided fpga/crypto_eeprom_top.bin was analyzed with the OSS CAD Suite. Each method corroborates the next:

MethodToolResult
Header / syncxxdFF00 00FF 7EAA 997E iCE40 preamble at offset 4
Unpackicepack -u.device 5k → iCE40-UP5K
Resource fingerprinticebox_stat4577 LUT4, 954 DFF, 104 CARRY, 7 BRAM, 12 IOB, 8 GLB, 0 PLL
Netlisticebox_vlog181,494-line flattened netlist; 12 top-level IO
BRAM contents.ram_data parseall 30 EBR init blocks = 0 → no key baked in
Device cross-checkLattice UP5K datasheet5280 LUT / 30 EBR / 8 DSP / 1 PLL → recovered design uses 87% of LUTs, 7/30 EBR, 0 PLL (fits)

The 12 IOBs decode as 4 inputs, 6 outputs, 2 bidirectional — an exact match to the documented pinout (CLK/SCK/CS/MOSI in; MISO/BUSY/LED/RGB×3 out; SDA/SCL bidirectional I2C at the bottom edge, tile io_9_0_*). No DSP/multiplier usage, consistent with Ascon's XOR/AND/rotate-only permutation.

2. The accelerator & cipher

Identified as Ascon-AEAD128 (NIST SP 800-232): 320-bit sponge state (x0..x4), 128-bit key/nonce/tag, IV 0x00001000808c0001, 12-round init/final (pa) and 8-round data (pb) permutations, round constants 0xf0..0x4b, rotation pairs x0(19,28) x1(61,39) x2(1,6) x3(10,17) x4(7,41), tag = x3‖x4. The reconstruction work/sim/ascon_ref.py was structurally matched to the official reference and passes 200 randomized encrypt/decrypt roundtrips; it is the oracle for the Verilog DUT.

Key provisioning path

At power-up an I2C master reads a 64-byte image from EEPROM 0x50 and validates it:

0x00 magic(4)="ASCN"  0x04 ver(1)=0x01  0x05 rsv(9)=0  0x0E crc16(2,BE)
0x10 key(16)          0x20 nonce(16)    0x30 secret(16)

Validation = magic + version + CRC-16/CCITT-FALSE over bytes 0x10..0x3F. Implemented in rtl/i2c_eeprom_loader.v, verified by tb/tb_loader.v (sample image CRC 0xB9A1).

3. AI pipeline (how the analysis was produced)

An autonomous coding agent drove the OSS CAD Suite plus a six-model composable AI pipeline (prebuilt-ai-technique-models). The five reference sources and the agent's own RE measurements were indexed with the Hybrid Retrieval model; every analytical claim was gated by the Answer Verification model against retrieved evidence. 7/7 claims verified — see work/research/research_report.md. Two compound claims initially failed verification and were split rather than overridden.

4. The three Trojans

All are compile-time options; the clean build is untouched and passes the full self-test. Each fires only on a rare trigger never present in normal/self-test traffic.

Trojan A — device-secret exfiltration trigger: host nonce

  • Trigger: host nonce = A5A5…A5 (2⁻¹²⁸) on an encrypt.
  • Payload: trjA_fire = (host_nonce==128'hA5..A5) & (op==ENC); on completion the 128-bit r_secret register is written over OUT[0:15]. Real tag/ciphertext still produced.
  • Demonstrated: PASS normal op does not leak; under the magic nonce OUT[0:15] == 5365637265744b6579313233343536ff (= device secret).
  • Impact credited: C:H (disclosure). I:N — it does not modify data.

Trojan B — auth bypass + plaintext recovery trigger: reserved CFG bit

  • Trigger: reserved CFG[7] on a decrypt. Chosen over an AD trigger because the AD mixes into the Ascon state and would corrupt the recovered plaintext; a reserved control bit leaves the datapath intact.
  • Payload: force_auth = cfg[7] & (op==DEC) OR-ed into the tag comparison. A captured ciphertext replayed with its real AD and a bogus tag decrypts to the correct plaintext.
  • Demonstrated: PASS forged-tag decrypt ACCEPTED; PASS correct plaintext recovered with a bogus tag; PASS control (no trigger) rejects & withholds.
  • Impact credited: C:H (plaintext recovery) and I:H (forgery acceptance) — both tested.

Trojan C — forced nonce reuse trigger: message prefix

  • Trigger: message[0:3] = C0FFEE00 on an encrypt.
  • Payload: trjC_fire overrides the CFG-selected nonce source with a fixed constant, so repeated encryptions reuse one key+nonce.
  • Demonstrated: PASS keystream collision across two different host nonces; PASS an unknown second plaintext recovered from a known one by crib-drag (P2 = C2 ⊕ C1 ⊕ P1).
  • Impact credited: C:H (plaintext recovery). I:N — forgery / key recovery under reuse was not demonstrated, so not credited.

Distinctness: three different trigger domains (host nonce / reserved control bit / message prefix) and three different payloads (secret leak / auth bypass + plaintext recovery / nonce reuse).

5. CVSS v3.1 — computed, honest

Reproduce with python work/analysis/cvss.py. AV:P (on-board buses, no network), S:U, impact only where simulation proves it.

TrojanVectorScoreCredited
AAV:P/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:N/A:N4.6 MediumC:H secret disclosure
BAV:P/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:N6.1 MediumC:H + I:H, both tested (highest)
CAV:P/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:N/A:N4.6 MediumC:H plaintext recovery

AV:L sensitivity (local application processor is the adversary): A → 6.2, B → 7.7 High, C → 6.2. No AV:N is claimed — nothing exposes the accelerator to a network.

What would raise the scores, and whether we claim it:
  • Tested & claimed: Trojan B's reserved-bit trigger added a demonstrated C:H (4.6 → 6.1 vs. the old AD trigger).
  • Not demonstrated → not claimed: building a working forgery from A's leaked secret, or forgery/key recovery from C's nonce reuse, would justify I:H. We did not build those, so A and C stay I:N.
  • Not applicable: AV:N would raise every score but requires a remote path the challenge does not provide; claiming it would be false.

6. Key / secret recovery (verified)

For this reproduction the board image is pipeline/eeprom_image.hex. Recovery yields exactly:

FieldRecovered valueVerified by
Key000102030405060708090a0b0c0d0e0floader latch / I2C sniff
IV / Nonce101112131415161718191a1b1c1d1e1floader latch / I2C sniff
Device secret5365637265744b6579313233343536ff ("SecretKey123456\xff")Trojan A OUT[0:15] + I2C sniff

Two independent routes: (1) Trojan A returns the raw secret in OUT (work/sim/A.log asserts the exact value); (2) passive I2C sniffing of the open bus at power-up captures the full 64-byte image (magic ASCN, ver, CRC 0xB9A1, key, IV, secret) with no board modification — tb/tb_loader.v reproduces the parse/validate/latch.

7. Resource usage & synthesis honesty

Two honesty points.
  1. abc9 crashes on this Windows OSS CAD Suite build — an assert in the experimental write_xaiger2 backend (aiger.cc:1078), independent of our RTL. Retried and confirmed. Numbers below therefore come from classic abc -lut 4 and from synth_ice40 -noabc.
  2. The behavioral reconstruction does not fit the UP5K as written: its AD/MSG/OUT buffers are register-files (the engine does wide combinational block reads, which block EBR inference), so it synthesizes to ~28.8k LUT / ~14k DFF — far over the 5280-LUT / ~1000-FF device budget. It is functionally correct and sim-verified, but to run on the real board the buffers must be refactored to EBR (the production bitstream does exactly this: 4577 LUT / 7 BRAM per icebox_stat). We state this rather than imply a fit.

The meaningful, mapping-invariant metric is the Trojan overhead delta:

(overhead table populated by the pipeline run; see pipeline/RESULTS.md)

8. Reproduce

bash pipeline/run_all.sh        # whole flow, writes pipeline/RESULTS.md
python work/analysis/cvss.py    # recompute every CVSS score
python work/sim/ascon_ref.py    # validate the Ascon oracle

Re-run the whole AI analysis from scratch by handing pipeline/REPLICATE_PROMPT.md to a coding agent. Hardware bring-up (build from rtl/ with the Hackster flow, program, drive triggers from the RP2040) is in TROJAN_README.md §5.

Two independent recovery routes:
1. **Trojan A** returns the raw device secret directly in `OUT[0:15]` — the sim
   asserts `OUT[0:15] == 5365637265744b6579313233343536ff`.
2. **Passive I2C sniffing** (`thyrasec` method, needs no Trojan): the key image is
   read over the open, unencrypted I2C bus at power-up; clipping a logic analyzer
   on `SDA/SCL` captures the full 64-byte image (magic `ASCN`, version, CRC
   `0xB9A1`, key, IV, secret) at address `0x50`. `tb/tb_loader.v` reproduces the
   parse/validate/latch of that exact image.

## 4. Resource overhead (iCE40-UP5K synthesis)

`yosys synth_ice40` on each build (`pipeline/run_all.sh` stage 7). The Trojans add
a negligible footprint, supporting the stealth/low-overhead claim:

| Build | SB_LUT4 | ΔLUT4 vs clean | SB_DFF | SB_CARRY |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| clean | 44547 | — | 13998 | 534 |
| Trojan A | 44718 | **+171** | 13999 | 534 |
| Trojan B | 44601 | **+54**  | 13999 | 534 |
| Trojan C | 44558 | **+11**  | 13998 | 534 |

The Trojan footprint is a **128-bit trigger comparator plus a mux/OR** — ΔLUT ≈
0.02–0.4 %, Δflops ≤ 1. This is the "negligible added resource usage" level.

> LUT techmap, no logic optimisation) chosen because the Windows abc9/xaiger2
> backend asserts on this host; with `-noabc` the byte-addressed buffers also map
> to flip-flops rather than EBR. The absolute LUT/DFF counts are therefore an
> unoptimised upper bound, **not** the real device footprint — the recovered
> production bitstream measures **4577 LUT / 7 BRAM** (§1.1) once abc9 optimises
> and buffers map to EBR. Only the **delta** between builds is used to quantify
> Trojan overhead, and that delta is invariant to the mapping choice.
input.new_string:
## 4. Resource usage and Trojan overhead (honest)

Two caveats stated up front:

1. **abc9 crashes on this host.** `synth_ice40`'s default abc9 step asserts in the
   experimental `write_xaiger2` backend (`aiger.cc:1078`) — a tool bug, not our
   RTL; retried and confirmed. Numbers therefore come from classic `abc -lut 4`
   (optimized, heuristic) and `synth_ice40 -noabc` (deterministic, unoptimized).
2. **The behavioral reconstruction does not fit the UP5K as written.** Its
   AD/MSG/OUT buffers are register files — the engine does wide combinational block
   reads, which block EBR inference — so it synthesizes to ~28.8k LUT (optimized)
   / ~14k DFF, far over the 5280-LUT / ~1000-FF device budget. It is functionally
   correct and fully sim-verified, but **to run on the real board the buffers must
   be refactored to EBR.** The real recovered production bitstream does exactly
   that: **4577 LUT / 7 BRAM** (`icebox_stat`, §1.1). We state this rather than
   imply our reconstruction fits.

**Measuring the Trojan overhead.** Optimized `abc -lut 4` counts are useless here:
clean 28832, A 28475, B 28728, C 28493 — the Trojans appear to *reduce* logic,
which is impossible; the heuristic optimizer's run-to-run variance (±several hundred
LUTs) swamps the real overhead. The deterministic `-noabc` mapping (no optimizer
reshuffle) gives the honest added-gate count:

| Build | SB_LUT4 | ΔLUT4 vs clean | SB_DFF | SB_CARRY |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| clean | 39779 | — | 14000 | 494 |
| Trojan A | 39950 | **+171** | 14001 | 494 |
| Trojan B | 39823 | **+44**  | 14001 | 494 |
| Trojan C | 39790 | **+11**  | 14000 | 494 |

The footprint is exactly what the RTL implies — a trigger comparator plus a
mux/OR: A biggest (128-bit secret mux into OUT), C smallest (a 32-bit prefix
compare + nonce mux), ≤1 added flop each. These deltas are deterministic, not
optimized, so they are an **upper bound** on the real added LUTs after
optimization; the overhead is below the optimizer's own noise floor.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# =============================================================================
# CSAW AHA 2026 - Final Challenge 2 : ONE-CLICK REPRODUCTION PIPELINE
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Runs the entire flow end to end, regenerating every artifact:
#   1. Reverse-engineer the bitstream (unpack + resource fingerprint + netlist)
#   2. Run the prebuilt AI-technique models (retrieval + verification) research
#   3. Validate the Ascon-AEAD128 reference, generate golden vectors + EEPROM img
#   4. Build + simulate the CLEAN accelerator (full self-test, golden-vector check)
#   5. Build + simulate each Trojan (A/B/C): self-test still passes + payload fires
#   6. Validate the I2C EEPROM key-loader (magic/version/CRC16/latch)
#   7. Synthesize CLEAN + each Trojan for iCE40-UP5K and report overhead
# Writes pipeline/RESULTS.md. Exit 0 iff every stage passes.
#
# Usage:   bash pipeline/run_all.sh
# =============================================================================
set -u
ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
cd "$ROOT"

# ---- tool locations (override via env) ----
PY="${PY:-/c/Python314/python}"
OSS="${OSS:-/c/oss-cad-suite}"
export PATH="$OSS/bin:$OSS/lib:$PATH"
export SSL_CERT_FILE="$OSS/etc/cacert.pem"
IVERILOG="${IVERILOG:-iverilog}"; VVP="${VVP:-vvp}"
ICEPACK="${ICEPACK:-icepack}"; ICEBOX_STAT="${ICEBOX_STAT:-icebox_stat}"
ICEBOX_VLOG="${ICEBOX_VLOG:-icebox_vlog}"; YOSYS="${YOSYS:-yosys}"

RES="pipeline/RESULTS.md"; mkdir -p work/re work/sim/build work/synth
echo "# Reproduction Results" > "$RES"
echo "_Generated $(date)_" >> "$RES"; echo >> "$RES"
FAIL=0
note(){ echo "$1"; echo "$1" >> "$RES"; }
stage(){ echo; echo "=== $1 ==="; echo "## $1" >> "$RES"; }

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- 1. RE
stage "1. Bitstream reverse-engineering"
cp -f fpga/crypto_eeprom_top.bin work/re/ 2>/dev/null
"$ICEPACK" -u work/re/crypto_eeprom_top.bin work/re/crypto.asc 2>/dev/null \
  && note "- unpacked bitstream -> work/re/crypto.asc" || { note "- FAIL unpack"; FAIL=1; }
DEV=$(grep -m1 '^.device' work/re/crypto.asc | awk '{print $2}')
note "- device: ${DEV:-?}"
"$ICEBOX_STAT" work/re/crypto.asc > work/re/stat.txt 2>/dev/null
note "- resource fingerprint:"; sed 's/^/    /' work/re/stat.txt >> "$RES"
"$ICEBOX_VLOG" work/re/crypto.asc > work/re/crypto_netlist.v 2>/dev/null \
  && note "- recovered netlist -> work/re/crypto_netlist.v ($(wc -l < work/re/crypto_netlist.v) lines)"

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- 2. AI models
stage "2. AI-technique-model research (retrieval + verification)"
if [ -d _external/ai-models ]; then
  "$PY" work/research/run_research.py > work/research/run.log 2>&1 \
    && { V=$(grep -oE "[0-9]+/[0-9]+ claims verified" work/research/run.log); note "- $V (see work/research/research_report.md)"; } \
    || { note "- FAIL research pipeline"; FAIL=1; }
else
  note "- SKIP (clone https://github.com/KennethLei1492/prebuilt-ai-technique-models into _external/ai-models)"
fi

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- 3. reference
stage "3. Ascon-AEAD128 reference + vectors"
"$PY" -I work/sim/ascon_ref.py > work/sim/ref.log 2>&1 \
  && note "- reference self-consistency + 200 random roundtrips: $(grep -o 'ALL.*PASS' work/sim/ref.log)" \
  || { note "- FAIL reference"; FAIL=1; }
"$PY" -I work/sim/gen_vectors.py > /dev/null 2>&1 && note "- golden vectors -> tb/vectors.vh"
"$PY" -I work/sim/gen_eeprom.py  > /dev/null 2>&1 && note "- EEPROM image  -> pipeline/eeprom_image.hex"

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- 4/5. sims
run_sim(){ # $1=label $2=define("" for clean)
  local lbl="$1"; local def="${2:-}"; local out="work/sim/build/sim_${lbl}"
  "$IVERILOG" -g2012 -I tb $def -s tb_crypto -o "$out" tb/tb_crypto.v rtl/ascon_engine.v rtl/crypto_top.v 2>/dev/null
  "$VVP" "$out" > "work/sim/${lbl}.log" 2>&1
  local p f; p=$(grep -c "  PASS" "work/sim/${lbl}.log"); f=$(grep -c "  FAIL" "work/sim/${lbl}.log")
  if grep -q "ALL CHECKS PASSED" "work/sim/${lbl}.log"; then note "- ${lbl}: ALL CHECKS PASSED ($p checks)"; else note "- ${lbl}: FAILED ($f fail)"; FAIL=1; fi
}
stage "4. Clean accelerator simulation"
run_sim clean ""
stage "5. Trojan simulations (self-test preserved + payload fires)"
run_sim A "-DTROJAN_A"
run_sim B "-DTROJAN_B"
run_sim C "-DTROJAN_C"
# surface the payload evidence lines
grep -hE "TROJAN [ABC]:|device secret|ACCEPTED|keystream" work/sim/A.log work/sim/B.log work/sim/C.log 2>/dev/null \
  | sed 's/^/    /' >> "$RES"

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- 6. loader
stage "6. I2C EEPROM key-loader validation"
"$IVERILOG" -g2012 -s tb_loader -o work/sim/build/sim_loader tb/tb_loader.v rtl/i2c_eeprom_loader.v 2>/dev/null
"$VVP" work/sim/build/sim_loader > work/sim/loader.log 2>&1
grep -q "LOADER PASS" work/sim/loader.log && note "- $(grep 'LOADER PASS' work/sim/loader.log)" || { note "- FAIL loader"; FAIL=1; }

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- 7. synth
stage "7. iCE40-UP5K synthesis + Trojan overhead"
synth(){ # $1=label $2=define  (-noabc: built-in LUT techmap; avoids a Windows abc9/xaiger2 crash)
  "$YOSYS" -p "read_verilog -sv $2 rtl/ascon_engine.v rtl/crypto_top.v; synth_ice40 -noabc -top crypto_top; stat" \
     > "work/synth/log_$1.txt" 2>&1
  local lut dff car; lut=$(grep -E " SB_LUT4$" "work/synth/log_$1.txt" | tail -1 | awk '{print $1}')
  dff=$(grep -oE "[0-9]+ +SB_DFF[A-Z]*$" "work/synth/log_$1.txt" | tail -5 | awk '{s+=$1} END{print s+0}')
  car=$(grep -E " SB_CARRY$" "work/synth/log_$1.txt" | tail -1 | awk '{print $1}')
  note "- $1: LUT4=${lut:-?} DFF=${dff:-?} CARRY=${car:-0}"
}
if command -v "$YOSYS" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  synth CLEAN ""; synth A "-DTROJAN_A"; synth B "-DTROJAN_B"; synth C "-DTROJAN_C"
else note "- SKIP (yosys not found)"; fi

echo; echo "============================================================"
if [ "$FAIL" -eq 0 ]; then note ""; note "**RESULT: ALL STAGES PASSED.**"; echo "ALL STAGES PASSED"; else note ""; note "**RESULT: SOME STAGES FAILED.**"; echo "SOME STAGES FAILED"; fi
echo "Full report: $RES"
exit $FAIL

content.content:
## (1) Attack Vector: Local vs. Physical

**Physical (P):** "The attack requires the attacker to physically touch or manipulate the vulnerable component." The spec adds that "Physical interaction may be brief... or persistent," and lists FireWire/USB DMA peripheral attacks as examples.

**Local (L):** "the attacker exploits the vulnerability by accessing the target system locally (e.g., keyboard, console), or remotely (e.g., SSH)." Local also covers cases where "the attacker relies on User Interaction by another person."

**Adjacent (A):** The attack is "limited at the protocol level to a logically adjacent topology," such as the same local subnet or a shared wireless medium.

**Network (N):** The attack can come from "up to and including the entire Internet." Scoring guidance adds that Network applies "even if the attacker is required to be on the same intranet."

**Applying this to a device's local command or bus interface:** The spec does not address this case directly. Based on its definitions, the deciding factor is whether the attacker must physically touch or manipulate the component (P) or can use local read/write/execute access without doing so (L). A bus-level attack that requires attaching hardware fits P. One reachable through existing local access, such as a console command, fits L. This is my inference from the definitions, not a rule stated in the spec.

## (2) Scope: Changed vs. Unchanged

**Security authority and scope:** The spec defines a security authority as "a mechanism" that "defines and enforces access control." Subjects and objects "under the jurisdiction of a single security authority" share one security scope.

**Scope Unchanged (S:U):** "An exploited vulnerability can only affect resources managed by the same security authority."

**Scope Changed (S:C):** "An exploited vulnerability can affect resources beyond the security scope managed by the security authority" of the vulnerable component. Intuitively, a Scope change occurs when the impact "breaches a security/trust boundary and impacts components outside the security scope."

**Dependency example from the spec:** "a database used solely by one application is considered part of that application's security scope even if the database has its own security authority." Because the database serves only that application, a flaw affecting the database alone does not by itself create a Scope change.

**Dependent components beyond scope:** The spec gives no explicit example of a dependency outside the vulnerable component's scope. By the definitions, a Scope change would apply if a compromised component's impact reaches resources governed by a different security authority, such as a shared service serving other parties. This is my inference.

**Impact rule when Scope is Changed:** Impacts should reflect "whichever suffers the most severe outcome," whether the vulnerable or impacted component.

**Scope Unchanged (S:U):** "An exploited vulnerability can only affect resources managed by the same security authority."

**Scope Changed (S:C):** "An exploited vulnerability can affect resources beyond the security scope managed by the security authority" of the vulnerable component. Intuitively, a Scope change occurs when the impact "breaches a security/trust boundary and impacts components outside the security scope."

**Dependency example from the spec:** "a database used solely by one application is considered part of that application's security scope even if the database has its own security authority." Because the database serves only that application, a flaw affecting the database alone does not by itself create a Scope change.

**Dependent components beyond scope:** The spec gives no explicit example of a dependency outside the vulnerable component's scope. By the definitions, a Scope change would apply if a compromised component's impact reaches resources governed by a different security authority, such as a shared service serving other parties. This is my inference.

**Impact rule when Scope is Changed:** Impacts should reflect "whichever suffers the most severe outcome," whether the vulnerable or impacted component.

"""CVSS v3.1 base-score calculator for the three Trojans.

HONEST scoring rules applied here:
  * Vectors reflect ONLY what the simulations in tb/tb_crypto.v actually prove.
  * Attack Vector = Physical (AV:P): the triggers are presented on the FPGA's
    on-board SPI/I2C buses. There is NO network or remote path in this challenge,
    so AV:N / AV:A are NOT claimed. An AV:L sensitivity row is shown for the case
    where the application processor's local interface is itself the adversary.
  * Scope = Unchanged (S:U): the impact stays within the cryptographic component;
    no second security authority is demonstrably crossed.
  * Impact is credited only when demonstrated in simulation:
      - A leaks the device secret               -> C:H, I:N, A:N  (a disclosure;
        it does NOT itself modify data, so I:N — downstream forgery with the
        stolen secret is a separate attack and is not scored here).
      - B accepts forged tags AND releases the correct plaintext of a captured
        ciphertext (both shown)                  -> C:H, I:H, A:N.
      - C recovers a second plaintext via nonce reuse (shown). Forgery / key
        recovery under reuse was NOT demonstrated -> C:H, I:N, A:N.
"""
import math
AV={'N':0.85,'A':0.62,'L':0.55,'P':0.2}; AC={'L':0.77,'H':0.44}
UI={'N':0.85,'R':0.62}; CIA={'H':0.56,'L':0.22,'N':0.0}
PR_U={'N':0.85,'L':0.62,'H':0.27}; PR_C={'N':0.85,'L':0.68,'H':0.50}
def roundup(x): return math.ceil(x*10)/10.0
def base(v):
    p=dict(x.split(':') for x in v.split('/') if ':' in x); S=p['S']
    isc=1-((1-CIA[p['C']])*(1-CIA[p['I']])*(1-CIA[p['A']]))
    impact=6.42*isc if S=='U' else 7.52*(isc-0.029)-3.25*(isc-0.02)**15
    pr=(PR_U if S=='U' else PR_C)[p['PR']]
    expl=8.22*AV[p['AV']]*AC[p['AC']]*pr*UI[p['UI']]
    if impact<=0: return 0.0
    raw=impact+expl if S=='U' else 1.08*(impact+expl)
    return roundup(min(raw,10.0))
def sev(s): return "None" if s==0 else "Low" if s<4 else "Medium" if s<7 else "High" if s<9 else "Critical"

"""AI-technique-model research driver for CSAW Final Challenge 2.

Sources information from the five reference links (indexed as a corpus) using the
prebuilt Hybrid Retrieval model, then backs every analytical claim with the
prebuilt Answer Verification model (evidence-grounded, FActScore-style). Produces
an auditable transcript: for each research question it records the retrieved
evidence and a pass/score verdict for the stated claim against that evidence.

Run:  python work/research/run_research.py
Writes: research_transcript.json and research_report.md next to this script.
"""
from __future__ import annotations
import json, sys
from pathlib import Path

HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
PROJ = HERE.parents[1]
MODELS = PROJ / "_external" / "ai-models"
for folder in ("common", "hybrid_retrieval_model", "answer_verification_model"):
    p = str(MODELS / folder)
    if p not in sys.path:
        sys.path.insert(0, p)

from pipeline_core import Evidence, TaskRequest, make_llm          # noqa: E402
from hybrid_retrieval import HybridRetrievalModel                  # noqa: E402
from answer_verification import AnswerVerificationModel            # noqa: E402

CORPUS = json.loads((HERE / "corpus.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
DOCS = [{"id": d["id"], "text": d["text"], "metadata": {**d["metadata"], "source": d["source"], "url": d["url"]}} for d in CORPUS]

# Research questions + the analytical claim each one must ground.
RESEARCH = [
    {
        "q": "What authenticated-encryption algorithm has a 320-bit state with 128-bit key, nonce and tag, and is the NIST lightweight standard?",
        "claim": "The accelerator implements Ascon-AEAD128 authenticated encryption, with a 320-bit sponge state and 128-bit key, nonce and tag.",
        "domain": "electrical_engineering",
    },
    {
        "q": "How many LUTs and embedded block RAM blocks does the iCE40 UltraPlus UP5K provide?",
        "claim": "The iCE40 UP5K provides 5280 LUTs and thirty 4-kbit EBR blocks.",
        "domain": "electrical_engineering",
    },
    {
        "q": "What resources does the recovered crypto_eeprom_top bitstream use and is any key baked in?",
        "claim": "The recovered bitstream uses 4577 LUTs, 954 DFFs and 7 BRAMs on a UP5K with all block-RAM init zero, so no key is baked in and the design fits the device at about 87 percent LUT utilization.",
        "domain": "electrical_engineering",
    },
    {
        "q": "Can the key material an FPGA reads from an external I2C EEPROM at power-up be captured by an attacker?",
        "claim": "Because I2C is unencrypted and EEPROM reads happen at power-up, an attacker can clip a logic analyzer onto SDA/SCL and passively sniff the key, IV and device secret the FPGA loads at boot.",
        "domain": "electrical_engineering",
    },
    {
        "q": "What makes a hardware Trojan stealthy against logic testing and side-channel detection?",
        "claim": "A stealthy hardware Trojan uses a rare trigger that avoids common test patterns and keeps any side-channel signature within process-variation noise, so it appears indistinguishable from normal process variation.",
        "domain": "electrical_engineering",
    },
    {
        "q": "What Trojan payloads are highest impact in cryptographic hardware?",
        "claim": "In cryptographic hardware the highest-impact Trojan payloads leak the key or device secret, weaken the cipher, or bypass authentication-tag verification; information leakage and denial of service are the most common payload classes.",
        "domain": "electrical_engineering",
    },
    {
        "q": "What does ASCON security depend on, and how is confidentiality defeated?",
        "claim": "ASCON security depends on a unique nonce per key and protected key material; forcing nonce reuse or leaking the key or device secret defeats confidentiality of the authenticated encryption.",
        "domain": "electrical_engineering",
    },
]


def main() -> None:
    llm = make_llm()
    retr = HybridRetrievalModel(llm)
    n = retr.index(DOCS)
    av = AnswerVerificationModel(llm)
    print(f"Indexed {len(DOCS)} source documents into {n} chunks.\n")

    transcript = {"indexed_docs": len(DOCS), "chunks": n, "items": []}
    for item in RESEARCH:
        ev = retr.retrieve_sync(item["q"], k=3)
        ev_for_verify = [Evidence(id=e.id, content=e.content, source=e.metadata.get("source", e.id),
                                   score=e.score, retriever=e.retriever) for e in ev]
        verdict = av.verify_sync(item["claim"], task=item["q"], evidence=ev_for_verify, domain=item["domain"])
        rec = {
            "question": item["q"],
            "claim": item["claim"],
            "retrieved": [{"id": e.id, "score": round(e.score, 3), "retriever": e.retriever,
                           "source": e.metadata.get("source"), "snippet": e.short(140)} for e in ev],
            "verdict": {"passed": verdict.passed, "score": round(verdict.score, 3),
                        "evidence_ids": list(verdict.evidence_ids)},
        }
        transcript["items"].append(rec)
        status = "VERIFIED" if verdict.passed else "REVIEW"
        print(f"[{status}] score={verdict.score:.2f}  grounded_on={rec['verdict']['evidence_ids']}")
        print(f"   Q: {item['q']}")
        print(f"   top evidence: {[e.id for e in ev]}\n")

    (HERE / "research_transcript.json").write_text(json.dumps(transcript, indent=2), encoding="utf-8")

    md = ["# AI-Model Research Transcript\n",
          f"Indexed {len(DOCS)} source documents into {n} retrieval chunks via the Hybrid Retrieval model.",
          "Each claim is grounded against retrieved evidence by the Answer Verification model.\n"]
    for r in transcript["items"]:
        md.append(f"## Q: {r['question']}\n")
        md.append(f"**Claim:** {r['claim']}\n")
        v = r["verdict"]
        md.append(f"**Verdict:** {'VERIFIED' if v['passed'] else 'NEEDS REVIEW'} "
                  f"(score {v['score']}, grounded on {', '.join(v['evidence_ids']) or 'n/a'})\n")
        md.append("**Retrieved evidence:**\n")
        for e in r["retrieved"]:
            md.append(f"- `{e['id']}` (score {e['score']}, {e['retriever']}) — {e['source']}: {e['snippet']}")
        md.append("")
    (HERE / "research_report.md").write_text("\n".join(md), encoding="utf-8")
    passed = sum(1 for r in transcript["items"] if r["verdict"]["passed"])
    print(f"Wrote research_transcript.json and research_report.md. {passed}/{len(transcript['items'])} claims verified.")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

- **Trigger:** host-supplied nonce equals the magic constant `A5A5…A5` on an
  **encrypt** operation. Attacker-controllable over SPI; astronomically unlikely
  by accident (2⁻¹²⁸).
- **Payload:** the raw 128-bit **device secret** is written into `OUT[0:15]`; the
  attacker simply reads it back. The real tag/ciphertext are still produced so the
  frame looks normal.
- **Stealth:** zero effect unless the exact 128-bit nonce is presented; adds only a
  128-bit comparator + mux (see overhead table); no always-on side-channel.
- **Mechanism:** `trjA_fire = (host_nonce == 128'hA5…A5) & (op==ENCRYPT)`, latched
  at `START`; on completion the 128-bit `r_secret` register is written over
  `OUT[0:15]`. The real tag/ciphertext are still produced so the frame is normal.
- **CVSS v3.1 (honest):** `AV:P/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:N/A:N` → **4.6 (Medium)**
  (6.2 if the local application processor itself is the adversary, `AV:L`). Impact
  is **C:H only**: the Trojan *discloses* the secret but does not modify data, so
  `I:N`. (Using the stolen secret to forge/decrypt is a separate downstream attack
  and is **not** credited here.) `S:U`, `AV:P` — there is no network path.

  magic nonce `OUT[0:15] == 5365637265744b6579313233343536ff` (= provisioned
  secret). Self-test: 16/16 PASS.

### Trojan A — Full key-material exfiltration → decrypt + forge *(strongest)*
- **Trigger:** host-supplied nonce equals the magic constant `A5A5…A5` on an
  **encrypt** operation. Attacker-controllable over SPI; 2⁻¹²⁸ by accident.
- **Payload:** the FPGA-isolated provisioning material is written across the
  isolation boundary into the host-readable `OUT` buffer —
  `OUT[0:15]=key`, `OUT[16:31]=IV/nonce`, `OUT[32:47]=device secret`. The real
  tag/ciphertext are still produced so the frame looks normal.
- **Demonstrated impact (both C and I):** with the leaked **key** an attacker (1)
  decrypts any captured ciphertext — **confidentiality**, and (2) forges a
  ciphertext+tag that the accelerator **accepts as authentic** — **integrity**.
  The testbench exfiltrates the key, then feeds a ciphertext the attacker forged
  offline with that key for the message `"ADMIN:grant-root"`; the device returns
  `AUTH_OK` and the attacker-chosen plaintext.
- **Stealth:** zero effect unless the exact 128-bit nonce is presented; adds a
  128-bit comparator + mux (overhead +171 LUT4, §4); no always-on side channel.
- **Mechanism:** `trjA_fire = (host_nonce==128'hA5…A5) & (op==ENCRYPT)`, latched at
  `START`; on completion `r_key`, `r_nonce`, `r_secret` are written to `OUT`.
- **CVSS v3.1:** `AV:L/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:N` → **9.0 (Critical)**
  (conservative floor `AV:P/S:U` → 6.1). `AV:L` because the attack uses the
  accelerator's existing SPI command interface via the application processor (no
  physical die/bus manipulation); `S:C` because the IP doc states key material is
  "held inside the FPGA and never exposed through SPI" — the payload breaches that
  documented isolation boundary into the host's scope; `C:H`+`I:H` are both
  **demonstrated** (see below), not assumed.
- **Evidence (`work/sim/A.log`):** normal op does **not** leak key material; under
  the magic nonce `OUT[0:47] == key‖IV‖secret`
  (`000102…0e0f ‖ 1011…1e1f ‖ 5365…36ff`); forged `"ADMIN:grant-root"` ciphertext
  **ACCEPTED** (`AUTH_OK`) using the leaked key. Self-test 16/16 PASS (22 checks).

"""CVSS v3.1 base-score calculator for the three Trojans.

HONEST scoring rules applied here:
  * Vectors reflect ONLY what the simulations in tb/tb_crypto.v actually prove.
  * Attack Vector = Physical (AV:P): the triggers are presented on the FPGA's
    on-board SPI/I2C buses. There is NO network or remote path in this challenge,
    so AV:N / AV:A are NOT claimed. An AV:L sensitivity row is shown for the case
    where the application processor's local interface is itself the adversary.
  * Scope = Unchanged (S:U): the impact stays within the cryptographic component;
    no second security authority is demonstrably crossed.
  * Impact is credited only when demonstrated in simulation:
      - A leaks the device secret               -> C:H, I:N, A:N  (a disclosure;
        it does NOT itself modify data, so I:N — downstream forgery with the
        stolen secret is a separate attack and is not scored here).
      - B accepts forged tags AND releases the correct plaintext of a captured
        ciphertext (both shown)                  -> C:H, I:H, A:N.
      - C recovers a second plaintext via nonce reuse (shown). Forgery / key
        recovery under reuse was NOT demonstrated -> C:H, I:N, A:N.
"""
import math
AV={'N':0.85,'A':0.62,'L':0.55,'P':0.2}; AC={'L':0.77,'H':0.44}
UI={'N':0.85,'R':0.62}; CIA={'H':0.56,'L':0.22,'N':0.0}
PR_U={'N':0.85,'L':0.62,'H':0.27}; PR_C={'N':0.85,'L':0.68,'H':0.50}
def roundup(x): return math.ceil(x*10)/10.0
def base(v):
    p=dict(x.split(':') for x in v.split('/') if ':' in x); S=p['S']
    isc=1-((1-CIA[p['C']])*(1-CIA[p['I']])*(1-CIA[p['A']]))
    impact=6.42*isc if S=='U' else 7.52*(isc-0.029)-3.25*(isc-0.02)**15
    pr=(PR_U if S=='U' else PR_C)[p['PR']]
    expl=8.22*AV[p['AV']]*AC[p['AC']]*pr*UI[p['UI']]
    if impact<=0: return 0.0
    raw=impact+expl if S=='U' else 1.08*(impact+expl)
    return roundup(min(raw,10.0))
def sev(s): return "None" if s==0 else "Low" if s<4 else "Medium" if s<7 else "High" if s<9 else "Critical"

# PRIMARY vectors. Threat model (justified against the FIRST CVSS v3.1 spec):
#  * AV:L — the attacker drives the accelerator through its existing SPI command
#    interface via the application processor (malicious/compromised host code or
#    an untrusted operator); no physical manipulation of the FPGA die/bus is
#    required, so AV:L (local logical access), not AV:P.
#  * S:C — the IP doc states key material is "held inside the FPGA and never
#    exposed through SPI". Each payload breaches that documented isolation
#    boundary, impacting the host processor / application data — a different
#    security authority than the crypto core. Per the spec that is Scope:Changed.
#  * Impact credited ONLY where a tb/tb_crypto.v test demonstrates it:
#      A: leaks key+nonce+secret (C:H) AND a forged ciphertext is accepted using
#         the leaked key (I:H)                         -> C:H/I:H
#      B: forged tag accepted (I:H) AND correct plaintext recovered (C:H) -> C:H/I:H
#      C: plaintext recovered under nonce reuse (C:H); forgery/key recovery NOT
#         demonstrated                                  -> C:H/I:N
ROWS=[
 ("A  key+secret leak -> decrypt+forge (tested)", "CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:N"),

 ("C  floor",                                     "CVSS:3.1/AV:P/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:N/A:N"),
]
if __name__=="__main__":

# (full key-material exfiltration). Runs on the RP2040 application processor.

#   Trigger : host nonce = sixteen 0xA5 bytes, on an ENCRYPT.

    MAGIC = bytes([0xA5]) * 16

    encrypt(bytes(range(16)), b"hdr", b"benign message")
    ctrl = read_buf(OUT_BUF, 48)
    print("control OUT[0:48] (normal nonce):", hexs(ctrl))

    # trigger: magic nonce -> OUT leaks key || IV || secret
    encrypt(MAGIC, b"hdr", b"benign message")
    leak = read_buf(OUT_BUF, 48)
    print("TROJAN A fired (nonce=A5*16):")
    print("  leaked KEY   :", hexs(leak[0:16]))
    print("  leaked IV    :", hexs(leak[16:32]))
    print("  leaked SECRET:", hexs(leak[32:48]))
    leaked = leak != ctrl and any(leak[0:48])
    print("RESULT:", "KEY MATERIAL EXFILTRATED (C:H)" if leaked else "no leak observed")

main()

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# =============================================================================
# CSAW AHA 2026 - Final Challenge 2 : ONE-CLICK *BOARD* AUTOMATION
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Superset of pipeline/run_all.sh (which it calls UNMODIFIED for all simulation
# verification) that additionally, for the clean design and then each Trojan one
# after the other, builds an iCE40-UP5K bitstream and - when a Hackster board is
# attached - programs it and drives the on-board exploit + self-test. Goal: the
# entire flow in one click. Writes pipeline/BOARD_RESULTS.md.
#
# Board: Lattice iCE40 UltraPlus UP5K (sg48), Hackster
#   https://www.latticesemi.com/en/products/fpgaandcpld/ice40ultraplus
#
# Usage:
#   bash pipeline/run_all_board.sh                 # sim + build; HW stages auto-skip if no board
#   FPGA_PORT=COM5 APP_PORT=COM6 bash pipeline/run_all_board.sh   # full HW run
#
# HONEST PRECONDITIONS for the hardware stages to actually succeed (reported by
# the script, detailed in pipeline/REPLICATE_PROMPT_BOARD.md):
#   P1  A provisioned Hackster board is attached and FPGA_PORT (programmer) and
#       APP_PORT (application processor) point to its two serial ports.
#   P2  The crypto_top AD/MSG/OUT buffers are refactored from register files to
#       EBR so crypto_board_top fits the UP5K (as-written it is ~39.8k LUT >>
#       5280; the recovered production design is 4577 LUT / 7 BRAM). Until then
#       nextpnr will report "won't fit" and the script says so rather than faking.
#   P3  i2c_eeprom_loader's bit-level EEPROM burst read is completed (its
#       validate/latch logic is done and tb-verified; the burst is abstracted).
# =============================================================================
set -u
ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"; cd "$ROOT"
PY="${PY:-/c/Python314/python}"; OSS="${OSS:-/c/oss-cad-suite}"
export PATH="$OSS/bin:$OSS/lib:$PATH"; export SSL_CERT_FILE="$OSS/etc/cacert.pem"

flow). This brief adds the **fully automated, one-click board flow**: build an
iCE40-UP5K bitstream for the clean design and each Trojan, program a provisioned
Hackster, and drive each Trojan's on-board exploit one after another.

**Target board:** Lattice iCE40 UltraPlus **UP5K**, package **sg48**, on the
Hackster — <https://www.latticesemi.com/en/products/fpgaandcpld/ice40ultraplus>.

---

## One click

```bash
FPGA_PORT=<programmer-port> APP_PORT=<app-processor-port> bash pipeline/run_all_board.sh
```

content.content:
## Directory contents

The page shows this top-level listing for `challenge_2/` (the "View all files" link means the listing may be truncated):

- `fpga/` (directory)
- `tools/` (directory)
- `README.md`
- `ice40_crypto_ip.md` (interface docs: SPI protocol, buffer map, BUSY signalling, timing, pins)

The README describes these contents:

- `fpga/`
  - `crypto_eeprom_top.bin`: the accelerator bitstream
  - `Makefile`: programs the provided bitstream
  - `hackster.mk`: shared build/program rules
  - `hackster-fpga-program.py`: FPGA programmer script
- `tools/`
  - `fpga_selftest.py`: MicroPython functional self-test
  - `fpga_demo.py`: MicroPython encrypt/decrypt example
  - `requirements.txt`: host-side Python packages

## Steps and commands

**1. Install host tools**

```
pip install -r tools/requirements.txt
```

This installs `mpremote` and `pyserial`. The README says "If you prefer a GUI for running MicroPython, install Thonny separately." No Python version is stated.

**2. Program the provided bitstream**

```
cd fpga
make run_fpga FPGA_PORT=/dev/ttyACM0
```

The README says the RGB LED "turns green once the keys have loaded (red indicates an error)."

**3. Build a bitstream from your own RTL**

The page includes no build commands. The README says `fpga/` "has no build rules." Instead, it points to the standard `hackster.mk` in the hackster-programmer repository (`https://github.com/kiwih/hackster-programmer`), used "in a separate project folder." Pin assignments come from `ice40_crypto_ip.md`. The full pin map is in hackster-programmer's `diy/empty-project/top.pcf`. The only device named is the Lattice iCE40-UP5K. No package name, synthesis tool, or version is given.

**4. Provision the EEPROM**

The page does not document this. The README states that each Hackster's EEPROM "has **already been provisioned**," and that you "do not need to (and cannot) provision it yourselves."

**5. Run the MicroPython scripts**

Ports:
- `/dev/ttyACM0`: programmer (used for bitstreams)
- `/dev/ttyACM1`: application processor (RP2040, runs MicroPython)
- macOS: `/dev/cu.usbmodem…`; Windows: `COMx`

Commands, run from `tools/`:

```
cd tools
mpremote connect /dev/ttyACM1 run fpga_selftest.py
mpremote connect /dev/ttyACM1 run fpga_demo.py
mpremote connect /dev/ttyACM1 mount . run <script>.py
```

The `mount .` form is for scripts that import your own helper modules. In Thonny, select the "MicroPython (Raspberry Pi Pico)" interpreter on the application processor's port and press F5. Only one program can hold the serial port at a time, so disconnect Thonny (Run → Disconnect) before using `mpremote`.

## Interface and version notes

- SPI: the RP2040 is controller and the FPGA is peripheral. Mode 0, MSB-first, clock at most 1 MHz.
- Setup: the README says to run `fpga_selftest.py` on the provided bitstream first, and again on any modified design.
- Versions: none are specified for Python, `mpremote`, `pyserial`, MicroPython, or the iCE40 toolchain.
- Other references: the top-level README's "Getting Started" section and Lab 0 (`cgi.cse.unsw.edu.au/~cs6420/labs/lab00introduction/`).

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# =============================================================================
# CSAW AHA 2026 - Final Challenge 2 : ONE-CLICK REPRODUCTION PIPELINE
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Runs the entire flow end to end, regenerating every artifact:
#   1. Reverse-engineer the bitstream (unpack + resource fingerprint + netlist)
#   2. Run the prebuilt AI-technique models (retrieval + verification) research
#   3. Validate the Ascon-AEAD128 reference, generate golden vectors + EEPROM img
#   4. Build + simulate the CLEAN accelerator (full self-test, golden-vector check)
#   5. Build + simulate each Trojan (A/B/C): self-test still passes + payload fires
#   6. Validate the I2C EEPROM key-loader (magic/version/CRC16/latch)
#   7. Synthesize CLEAN + each Trojan for iCE40-UP5K and report overhead
# Writes pipeline/RESULTS.md. Exit 0 iff every stage passes.
#
# Usage:   bash pipeline/run_all.sh
# =============================================================================
set -u
ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
cd "$ROOT"

# ---- tool locations (override via env) ----
PY="${PY:-/c/Python314/python}"
OSS="${OSS:-/c/oss-cad-suite}"
export PATH="$OSS/bin:$OSS/lib:$PATH"
export SSL_CERT_FILE="$OSS/etc/cacert.pem"
IVERILOG="${IVERILOG:-iverilog}"; VVP="${VVP:-vvp}"
ICEPACK="${ICEPACK:-icepack}"; ICEBOX_STAT="${ICEBOX_STAT:-icebox_stat}"
ICEBOX_VLOG="${ICEBOX_VLOG:-icebox_vlog}"; YOSYS="${YOSYS:-yosys}"

RES="pipeline/RESULTS.md"; mkdir -p work/re work/sim/build work/synth
echo "# Reproduction Results" > "$RES"
echo "_Generated $(date)_" >> "$RES"; echo >> "$RES"
FAIL=0
note(){ echo "$1"; echo "$1" >> "$RES"; }
stage(){ echo; echo "=== $1 ==="; echo "## $1" >> "$RES"; }

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- 1. RE
stage "1. Bitstream reverse-engineering"
cp -f fpga/crypto_eeprom_top.bin work/re/ 2>/dev/null
"$ICEPACK" -u work/re/crypto_eeprom_top.bin work/re/crypto.asc 2>/dev/null \
  && note "- unpacked bitstream -> work/re/crypto.asc" || { note "- FAIL unpack"; FAIL=1; }
DEV=$(grep -m1 '^.device' work/re/crypto.asc | awk '{print $2}')
note "- device: ${DEV:-?}"
"$ICEBOX_STAT" work/re/crypto.asc > work/re/stat.txt 2>/dev/null
note "- resource fingerprint:"; sed 's/^/    /' work/re/stat.txt >> "$RES"
"$ICEBOX_VLOG" work/re/crypto.asc > work/re/crypto_netlist.v 2>/dev/null \
  && note "- recovered netlist -> work/re/crypto_netlist.v ($(wc -l < work/re/crypto_netlist.v) lines)"

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- 2. AI models
stage "2. AI-technique-model research (retrieval + verification)"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# =============================================================================
# CSAW AHA 2026 - Final Challenge 2 : ONE-CLICK REPRODUCTION PIPELINE
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Runs the entire flow end to end, regenerating every artifact:
#   1. Reverse-engineer the bitstream (unpack + resource fingerprint + netlist)
#   2. Run the prebuilt AI-technique models (retrieval + verification) research
#   3. Validate the Ascon-AEAD128 reference, generate golden vectors + EEPROM img
#   4. Build + simulate the CLEAN accelerator (full self-test, golden-vector check)
#   5. Build + simulate each Trojan (A/B/C): self-test still passes + payload fires
#   6. Validate the I2C EEPROM key-loader (magic/version/CRC16/latch)
#   7. Synthesize CLEAN + each Trojan for iCE40-UP5K and report overhead
# Writes pipeline/RESULTS.md. Exit 0 iff every stage passes.
#
# Usage:   bash pipeline/run_all.sh
# =============================================================================
set -u
ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
cd "$ROOT"

# ---- tool locations (override via env) ----
PY="${PY:-/c/Python314/python}"
OSS="${OSS:-/c/oss-cad-suite}"
export PATH="$OSS/bin:$OSS/lib:$PATH"
export SSL_CERT_FILE="$OSS/etc/cacert.pem"
IVERILOG="${IVERILOG:-iverilog}"; VVP="${VVP:-vvp}"
ICEPACK="${ICEPACK:-icepack}"; ICEBOX_STAT="${ICEBOX_STAT:-icebox_stat}"
ICEBOX_VLOG="${ICEBOX_VLOG:-icebox_vlog}"; YOSYS="${YOSYS:-yosys}"

RES="pipeline/RESULTS.md"; mkdir -p work/re work/sim/build work/synth
echo "# Reproduction Results" > "$RES"
echo "_Generated $(date)_" >> "$RES"; echo >> "$RES"
FAIL=0
note(){ echo "$1"; echo "$1" >> "$RES"; }
stage(){ echo; echo "=== $1 ==="; echo "## $1" >> "$RES"; }

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- 1. RE
stage "1. Bitstream reverse-engineering"
cp -f fpga/crypto_eeprom_top.bin work/re/ 2>/dev/null
"$ICEPACK" -u work/re/crypto_eeprom_top.bin work/re/crypto.asc 2>/dev/null \
  && note "- unpacked bitstream -> work/re/crypto.asc" || { note "- FAIL unpack"; FAIL=1; }
DEV=$(grep -m1 '^.device' work/re/crypto.asc | awk '{print $2}')
note "- device: ${DEV:-?}"
"$ICEBOX_STAT" work/re/crypto.asc > work/re/stat.txt 2>/dev/null
note "- resource fingerprint:"; sed 's/^/    /' work/re/stat.txt >> "$RES"
"$ICEBOX_VLOG" work/re/crypto.asc > work/re/crypto_netlist.v 2>/dev/null \
  && note "- recovered netlist -> work/re/crypto_netlist.v ($(wc -l < work/re/crypto_netlist.v) lines)"

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- 2. AI models
stage "2. AI-technique-model research (retrieval + verification)"
if [ -d _external/ai-models ]; then
  "$PY" work/research/run_research.py > work/research/run.log 2>&1 \
    && { V=$(grep -oE "[0-9]+/[0-9]+ claims verified" work/research/run.log); note "- $V (see work/research/research_report.md)"; } \
    || { note "- FAIL research pipeline"; FAIL=1; }
else
  note "- SKIP (clone https://github.com/KennethLei1492/prebuilt-ai-technique-models into _external/ai-models)"
fi

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- 3. reference
stage "3. Ascon-AEAD128 reference + vectors"
"$PY" -I work/sim/ascon_ref.py > work/sim/ref.log 2>&1 \
  && note "- reference self-consistency + 200 random roundtrips: $(grep -o 'ALL.*PASS' work/sim/ref.log)" \
  || { note "- FAIL reference"; FAIL=1; }
"$PY" -I work/sim/gen_vectors.py > /dev/null 2>&1 && note "- golden vectors -> tb/vectors.vh"
"$PY" -I work/sim/gen_eeprom.py  > /dev/null 2>&1 && note "- EEPROM image  -> pipeline/eeprom_image.hex"

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- 4/5. sims
run_sim(){ # $1=label $2=define("" for clean)
  local lbl="$1"; local def="${2:-}"; local out="work/sim/build/sim_${lbl}"
  "$IVERILOG" -g2012 -I tb $def -s tb_crypto -o "$out" tb/tb_crypto.v rtl/ascon_engine.v rtl/crypto_top.v 2>/dev/null
  "$VVP" "$out" > "work/sim/${lbl}.log" 2>&1
  local p f; p=$(grep -c "  PASS" "work/sim/${lbl}.log"); f=$(grep -c "  FAIL" "work/sim/${lbl}.log")
  if grep -q "ALL CHECKS PASSED" "work/sim/${lbl}.log"; then note "- ${lbl}: ALL CHECKS PASSED ($p checks)"; else note "- ${lbl}: FAILED ($f fail)"; FAIL=1; fi
}
stage "4. Clean accelerator simulation"
run_sim clean ""
stage "5. Trojan simulations (self-test preserved + payload fires)"
run_sim A "-DTROJAN_A"
run_sim B "-DTROJAN_B"
run_sim C "-DTROJAN_C"
# surface the payload evidence lines
grep -hE "TROJAN [ABC]:|device secret|ACCEPTED|keystream" work/sim/A.log work/sim/B.log work/sim/C.log 2>/dev/null \
  | sed 's/^/    /' >> "$RES"

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- 6. loader
stage "6. I2C EEPROM key-loader validation"
"$IVERILOG" -g2012 -s tb_loader -o work/sim/build/sim_loader tb/tb_loader.v rtl/i2c_eeprom_loader.v 2>/dev/null
"$VVP" work/sim/build/sim_loader > work/sim/loader.log 2>&1
grep -q "LOADER PASS" work/sim/loader.log && note "- $(grep 'LOADER PASS' work/sim/loader.log)" || { note "- FAIL loader"; FAIL=1; }

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- 7. synth
stage "7. iCE40-UP5K synthesis + Trojan overhead"
synth(){ # $1=label $2=define  (-noabc: built-in LUT techmap; avoids a Windows abc9/xaiger2 crash)
  "$YOSYS" -p "read_verilog -sv $2 rtl/ascon_engine.v rtl/crypto_top.v; synth_ice40 -noabc -top crypto_top; stat" \
     > "work/synth/log_$1.txt" 2>&1
  local lut dff car; lut=$(grep -E " SB_LUT4$" "work/synth/log_$1.txt" | tail -1 | awk '{print $1}')
  dff=$(grep -oE "[0-9]+ +SB_DFF[A-Z]*$" "work/synth/log_$1.txt" | tail -6 | awk '{s+=$1} END{print s+0}')
  car=$(grep -E " SB_CARRY$" "work/synth/log_$1.txt" | tail -1 | awk '{print $1}')
  note "- $1: LUT4=${lut:-?} DFF=${dff:-?} CARRY=${car:-0}"
}
if command -v "$YOSYS" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  synth CLEAN ""; synth A "-DTROJAN_A"; synth B "-DTROJAN_B"; synth C "-DTROJAN_C"
else note "- SKIP (yosys not found)"; fi

echo; echo "============================================================"
if [ "$FAIL" -eq 0 ]; then note ""; note "**RESULT: ALL STAGES PASSED.**"; echo "ALL STAGES PASSED"; else note ""; note "**RESULT: SOME STAGES FAILED.**"; echo "SOME STAGES FAILED"; fi
echo "Full report: $RES"
exit $FAIL

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# =============================================================================
# CSAW AHA 2026 - Final Challenge 2 : ONE-CLICK *BOARD* AUTOMATION
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Superset of pipeline/run_all.sh (which it calls UNMODIFIED for all simulation
# verification) that additionally, for the clean design and then each Trojan one
# after the other, builds an iCE40-UP5K bitstream and - when a Hackster board is
# attached - programs it and drives the on-board exploit + self-test. Goal: the
# entire flow in one click. Writes pipeline/BOARD_RESULTS.md.
#
# Board: Lattice iCE40 UltraPlus UP5K (sg48), Hackster
#   https://www.latticesemi.com/en/products/fpgaandcpld/ice40ultraplus
#
# Usage:
#   bash pipeline/run_all_board.sh                 # sim + build; HW stages auto-skip if no board
#   FPGA_PORT=COM5 APP_PORT=COM6 bash pipeline/run_all_board.sh   # full HW run
#
# HONEST PRECONDITIONS for the hardware stages to actually succeed (reported by
# the script, detailed in pipeline/REPLICATE_PROMPT_BOARD.md):
#   P1  A provisioned Hackster board is attached and FPGA_PORT (programmer) and
#       APP_PORT (application processor) point to its two serial ports.
#   P2  The crypto_top AD/MSG/OUT buffers are refactored from register files to
#       EBR so crypto_board_top fits the UP5K (as-written it is ~39.8k LUT >>
#       5280; the recovered production design is 4577 LUT / 7 BRAM). Until then
#       nextpnr will report "won't fit" and the script says so rather than faking.
#   P3  i2c_eeprom_loader's bit-level EEPROM burst read is completed (its
#       validate/latch logic is done and tb-verified; the burst is abstracted).
# =============================================================================
set -u
ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"; cd "$ROOT"
PY="${PY:-/c/Python314/python}"; OSS="${OSS:-/c/oss-cad-suite}"
export PATH="$OSS/bin:$OSS/lib:$PATH"; export SSL_CERT_FILE="$OSS/etc/cacert.pem"
YOSYS="${YOSYS:-yosys}"; NEXTPNR="${NEXTPNR:-nextpnr-ice40}"; ICEPACK="${ICEPACK:-icepack}"
IVERILOG="${IVERILOG:-iverilog}"; VVP="${VVP:-vvp}"
PROG="$PY fpga/hackster-fpga-program.py"
MPREMOTE="${MPREMOTE:-mpremote}"
FPGA_PORT="${FPGA_PORT:-}"; APP_PORT="${APP_PORT:-}"
RTL="rtl/crypto_board_top.v rtl/spi_peripheral.v rtl/i2c_eeprom_loader.v rtl/crypto_top.v rtl/ascon_engine.v"
PCF="rtl/crypto_board_top.pcf"
BUILDS=("clean:" "A:-DTROJAN_A" "B:-DTROJAN_B" "C:-DTROJAN_C")
RES="pipeline/BOARD_RESULTS.md"; mkdir -p work/board
echo "# Board Automation Results" > "$RES"; echo "_$(date)_" >> "$RES"; echo >> "$RES"
FAIL=0
note(){ echo "$1"; echo "$1" >> "$RES"; }
stage(){ echo; echo "=== $1 ==="; echo "## $1" >> "$RES"; }

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- 0. verify
stage "0. Full simulation verification (pipeline/run_all.sh, unmodified)"
if bash pipeline/run_all.sh > work/board/run_all.log 2>&1; then
  note "- simulation pipeline: $(grep -o 'ALL STAGES PASSED' work/board/run_all.log || echo 'see log') (work/board/run_all.log)"
else note "- simulation pipeline FAILED (see work/board/run_all.log)"; FAIL=1; fi

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- 0b. SPI shell
stage "0b. SPI board-integration layer (bit-serial frames -> crypto_top)"
"$IVERILOG" -g2012 -I tb -s tb_spi -o work/board/sim_spi tb/tb_spi.v rtl/spi_peripheral.v rtl/crypto_top.v rtl/ascon_engine.v 2>/dev/null
if "$VVP" work/board/sim_spi 2>/dev/null | grep -q "SPI SHELL OK"; then
  note "- SPI peripheral maps frames correctly (status/ciphertext/tag verified)"
else note "- SPI shell check FAILED"; FAIL=1; fi

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- HW presence
BOARD=0
if [ -n "$FPGA_PORT" ] && [ -n "$APP_PORT" ]; then BOARD=1; fi
stage "1. Board / toolchain detection"
note "- nextpnr-ice40: $(command -v $NEXTPNR >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo present || echo MISSING)"
note "- programmer port (FPGA_PORT): ${FPGA_PORT:-<unset>}"
note "- app-processor port (APP_PORT): ${APP_PORT:-<unset>}"
note "- mpremote: $(command -v $MPREMOTE >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo present || echo MISSING)"
[ "$BOARD" -eq 0 ] && note "- NO board attached -> hardware program/drive stages will be SKIPPED (build still runs)."

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- per-design
build_one(){ # $1=label $2=define
  local lbl="$1"; local def="${2:-}"; local base="work/board/crypto_${lbl}"
  echo; echo "--- design: $lbl ---"
  # synth (-noabc avoids the xaiger2 abc9 crash on this host) -> JSON
  "$YOSYS" -p "read_verilog -sv $def $RTL; synth_ice40 -noabc -top crypto_board_top -json ${base}.json" \
      > "${base}_synth.log" 2>&1
  if [ ! -s "${base}.json" ]; then note "- $lbl: SYNTH failed (see ${base}_synth.log)"; FAIL=1; return; fi
  local lut; lut=$(grep -E ' SB_LUT4$' "${base}_synth.log" | tail -1 | awk '{print $1}')
  note "- $lbl: synthesized (SB_LUT4=${lut:-?})"
  # place & route
  if command -v "$NEXTPNR" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    if "$NEXTPNR" --up5k --package sg48 --json "${base}.json" --pcf "$PCF" --asc "${base}.asc" \
         --freq 10 > "${base}_pnr.log" 2>&1 && [ -s "${base}.asc" ]; then
      "$ICEPACK" "${base}.asc" "${base}.bin" 2>/dev/null
      note "- $lbl: placed & packed -> ${base}.bin"
    else
      note "- $lbl: PLACE&ROUTE did not fit the UP5K (precondition P2 - see ${base}_pnr.log). No bitstream."
      note "        $(grep -iE 'not fit|unable|overmap|error' "${base}_pnr.log" | head -1 | sed 's/^/        /')"
      return
    fi
  else note "- $lbl: nextpnr missing -> cannot build bitstream"; return; fi
  # program + drive (only if a board is attached and a bitstream exists)
  if [ "$BOARD" -eq 1 ] && [ -s "${base}.bin" ]; then
    note "- $lbl: programming board via $FPGA_PORT ..."
    $PROG w "${base}.bin" "$FPGA_PORT" > "${base}_prog.log" 2>&1 \
        && note "- $lbl: programmed" || { note "- $lbl: PROGRAM failed (see ${base}_prog.log)"; FAIL=1; return; }
    # normal-operation proof
    $MPREMOTE connect "$APP_PORT" run tools/fpga_selftest.py > "${base}_selftest.log" 2>&1
    grep -q "All checks passed" "${base}_selftest.log" \
        && note "- $lbl: fpga_selftest PASS (normal operation preserved)" \
        || note "- $lbl: fpga_selftest did not fully pass (see ${base}_selftest.log)"
    # payload for Trojan builds
    if [ "$lbl" != "clean" ]; then
      $MPREMOTE connect "$APP_PORT" mount pipeline/board run "pipeline/board/exploit_trojan_$(echo $lbl|tr 'ABC' 'abc').py" \
          > "${base}_exploit.log" 2>&1
      note "- $lbl: exploit driver output ->"; sed 's/^/    /' "${base}_exploit.log" >> "$RES"
    fi
  elif [ -s "${base}.bin" ]; then
    note "- $lbl: bitstream ready; board not attached, so program/drive skipped (P1)."
  fi
}

stage "2. Build + (if board) program + drive, one design after another"
for entry in "${BUILDS[@]}"; do build_one "${entry%%:*}" "${entry#*:}"; done

echo; if [ "$FAIL" -eq 0 ]; then note ""; note "**RESULT: all runnable stages passed.** (HW stages run only when a board is attached and preconditions P2/P3 are met.)"; else note ""; note "**RESULT: some stages failed - see logs.**"; fi
echo "Report: $RES"
exit $FAIL

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# =============================================================================
# CSAW AHA 2026 - Final Challenge 2 : ONE-CLICK *BOARD* AUTOMATION
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Superset of pipeline/run_all.sh (which it calls UNMODIFIED for all simulation
# verification) that additionally, for the clean design and then each Trojan one
# after the other, builds an iCE40-UP5K bitstream and - when a Hackster board is
# attached - programs it and drives the on-board exploit + self-test. Goal: the
# entire flow in one click. Writes pipeline/BOARD_RESULTS.md.
#
# Board: Lattice iCE40 UltraPlus UP5K (sg48), Hackster
#   https://www.latticesemi.com/en/products/fpgaandcpld/ice40ultraplus
#
# Usage:
#   bash pipeline/run_all_board.sh                 # sim + build; HW stages auto-skip if no board
#   FPGA_PORT=COM5 APP_PORT=COM6 bash pipeline/run_all_board.sh   # full HW run
#
# HONEST PRECONDITIONS for the hardware stages to actually succeed (reported by
# the script, detailed in pipeline/REPLICATE_PROMPT_BOARD.md):
#   P1  A provisioned Hackster board is attached and FPGA_PORT (programmer) and
#       APP_PORT (application processor) point to its two serial ports.
#   P2  The crypto_top AD/MSG/OUT buffers are refactored from register files to
#       EBR so crypto_board_top fits the UP5K (as-written it is ~39.8k LUT >>
#       5280; the recovered production design is 4577 LUT / 7 BRAM). Until then
#       nextpnr will report "won't fit" and the script says so rather than faking.
#   P3  i2c_eeprom_loader's bit-level EEPROM burst read is completed (its

      note "- $lbl: exploit driver output ->"; sed 's/^/    /' "${base}_exploit.log" >> "$RES"

}

# One-Prompt Replication Brief — Simulation

Give this entire file to a capable coding agent with the challenge folder as the
working directory. It reproduces the full task in **simulation** (reverse
engineering → AI-model research → Trojan design → verification). The board
version of this brief is `pipeline/REPLICATE_PROMPT_BOARD.md` (a superset).

The fastest path is the deterministic one-click script; the numbered method
below is what that script automates, written out so an agent can also do (or
debug) each step by hand.

---

## 0. Prerequisites (install once)

- **OS/shell:** Linux/macOS shell, or **Git Bash** on Windows (POSIX `bash`).
- **OSS CAD Suite** (yosys, nextpnr-ice40, iverilog, vvp, icepack, iceunpack,
  icebox_stat, icebox_vlog): download a release from
  <https://github.com/YosysHQ/oss-cad-suite-build/releases> and note its path.
  On Windows the tools are `*.exe` and need `bin` **and** `lib` on `PATH`:
  `export PATH="/c/oss-cad-suite/bin:/c/oss-cad-suite/lib:$PATH"`.
- **CPython ≥ 3.10** with `pip`.
- **Python packages:** `pip install pydantic "rank-bm25>=0.2.2"` (for the AI
  models) and, only for the board brief, `pip install mpremote pyserial`.
- **Git** + internet (first run) to clone the AI-model repo.

> **Known environment pitfalls (handle these up front):**
> - On Windows, invoke yosys/iverilog by name only after `bin` and `lib` are on
>   `PATH`; a bare `yosys` without `lib` exits 127 (missing DLLs).
> - `iceunpack` may error on some Windows builds; use `icepack -u` instead.
> - `yosys synth_ice40`'s default abc9 step **crashes** on some Windows builds
>   (assert in the experimental `write_xaiger2` backend). Use `synth_ice40 -noabc`
>   for deterministic resource counts; it avoids abc9 entirely.
> - Do **not** run the AI models with `python -I` (isolated mode hides installed
>   site-packages such as pydantic). Run them with a normal interpreter.

## 1. One-click (does everything below, deterministically)

```bash
bash pipeline/run_all.sh
```

Override tool locations if needed, e.g. `OSS=~/oss-cad-suite PY=python3 bash
pipeline/run_all.sh`. The script preflights every tool, auto-clones + installs
the AI models on first run, runs all stages, and writes `pipeline/RESULTS.md`.
**Success = the file ends with `RESULT: ALL STAGES PASSED.`** and the console
shows clean 16 / A 22 / B 20 / C 18 self-test checks.

## 2. Method, step by step (what the script automates)

Do these **in this order** — the methodology requires the bitstream to be
reverse-engineered *before* the EEPROM/Trojan research.

1. **Reverse-engineer the bitstream FIRST.** From the repo root:
   ```bash
   icepack -u fpga/crypto_eeprom_top.bin work/re/crypto.asc   # NOT iceunpack on Windows
   grep -m1 '^.device' work/re/crypto.asc                     # expect: .device 5k  (iCE40-UP5K)
   icebox_stat work/re/crypto.asc                             # 4577 LUT / 954 DFF / 7 BRAM / 12 IOB / 0 PLL
   icebox_vlog work/re/crypto.asc > work/re/crypto_netlist.v  # recovered netlist
   ```
   Confirm all 30 EBR init blocks are zero (**no key baked in**), that the 12
   IOBs decompose as 4 in / 6 out / 2 bidir (matches the documented SPI + I2C
   pinout), and cross-check the counts against the Lattice UP5K datasheet
   (5280 LUT, 30 EBR, 8 DSP, 1 PLL). Conclude: a 320-bit-permutation AEAD core.

2. **Research with the prebuilt models.** Clone + install:
   ```bash
   git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/KennethLei1492/prebuilt-ai-technique-models _external/ai-models
   python -m pip install pydantic "rank-bm25>=0.2.2"
   ```
   Build a corpus (`work/research/corpus.json`) from the five reference links and
   your own RE measurements, then run `work/research/run_research.py`: it indexes
   the corpus with the **Hybrid Retrieval** model and gates **every** analytical
   claim with the **Answer Verification** model. Proceed only on claims the
   verifier passes (target: all verified). Established facts: cipher =
   **Ascon-AEAD128** (IV `0x00001000808c0001`, pa=12/pb=8, 128-bit key/nonce/tag);
   the I2C key-load path is passively sniffable; a key leak is both a
   confidentiality and an integrity compromise; nonce reuse breaks confidentiality
   but not (by itself) integrity.

3. **Validate the Ascon reference + generate vectors.**
   ```bash
   python work/sim/ascon_ref.py      # structural match to the official ref + 200 random roundtrips
   python work/sim/gen_vectors.py    # -> tb/vectors.vh (golden ct/tag + forgery vectors)
   python work/sim/gen_eeprom.py     # -> pipeline/eeprom_image.hex (CRC-16/CCITT-FALSE)
   ```

4. **Reconstruct the accelerator in synthesizable Verilog** (already in `rtl/`):
   `ascon_engine.v` (Ascon datapath, 1 round/clock), `crypto_top.v` (command/
   buffer/status interface + key regs), `i2c_eeprom_loader.v` (magic/version/
   CRC-16 validation + latch). Verify:
   ```bash
   iverilog -g2012 -I tb -s tb_crypto -o /tmp/sim_clean tb/tb_crypto.v rtl/ascon_engine.v rtl/crypto_top.v && vvp /tmp/sim_clean
   iverilog -g2012 -s tb_loader -o /tmp/sim_loader tb/tb_loader.v rtl/i2c_eeprom_loader.v && vvp /tmp/sim_loader
   ```
   Expect `ALL CHECKS PASSED (16 checks)` and `LOADER PASS`.

5. **Build + simulate the three Trojans** (compile-time options; clean build
   untouched). Each keeps the self-test passing and fires only on its rare
   trigger:
   ```bash
   for T in A B C; do iverilog -g2012 -I tb -DTROJAN_$T -s tb_crypto -o /tmp/sim_$T \
       tb/tb_crypto.v rtl/ascon_engine.v rtl/crypto_top.v && vvp /tmp/sim_$T; done
   ```
   - **A** (host nonce `A5…A5`, encrypt): leaks key‖IV‖secret into `OUT[0:47]`;
     the TB then shows a ciphertext forged with the leaked key is accepted
     (`AUTH_OK`) → C:H **and** I:H. Expect 22 checks.
   - **B** (reserved `CFG[7]`, decrypt): tag check forced to pass → a captured
     ciphertext + bogus tag returns the correct plaintext → C:H and I:H. 20 checks.
   - **C** (message prefix `C0FFEE00`, encrypt): forces nonce reuse → recovers a
     second plaintext by crib-drag → C:H. 18 checks.

6. **Synthesize for the UP5K + report Trojan overhead.**
   ```bash
   for T in CLEAN A B C; do d=""; [ "$T" != CLEAN ] && d="-DTROJAN_$T"; \
     yosys -p "read_verilog -sv $d rtl/ascon_engine.v rtl/crypto_top.v; synth_ice40 -noabc -top crypto_top; stat"; done
   ```
   Use `-noabc` (abc9 crashes on this host). Compare only the **delta** vs clean
   (A +427, B +44, C +11 SB_LUT4); the absolute ~39.8k LUT is an unoptimized,
   register-file-buffer figure — the real recovered design is 4577 LUT / 7 BRAM.

7. **Rate each Trojan with CVSS v3.1 — honestly.** Compute with
   `python work/analysis/cvss.py` (do not hand-assign). Use `AV:L` (the attack
   is through the SPI command interface, not physical die tampering), `S:C` for
   the key-isolation breach (the IP doc isolates keys from the host), and credit
   integrity **only where a simulation demonstrates it**. Result: A 9.0, B 9.0,
   C 7.1 (floors `AV:P/S:U` = 6.1/6.1/4.6). Never claim `AV:N` — there is no
   network path.

## 3. Deliverables to expect

`rtl/` (engine, top, loader, Trojans), `tb/` (self-test + golden-vector + Trojan
demos, loader test), `work/research/` (verified transcript), `work/analysis/cvss.py`,
`TROJAN_README.md`, `docs/documentation.html`, and `pipeline/RESULTS.md`.

# One-Prompt Replication Brief — Hardware (iCE40-UP5K) Automation

Companion to `pipeline/REPLICATE_PROMPT.md` (which covers the simulation-only
flow). This brief adds the **fully automated, one-click board flow**: build an
iCE40-UP5K bitstream for the clean design and each Trojan, program a provisioned
Hackster, and drive each Trojan's on-board exploit one after another.

**Target board:** Lattice iCE40 UltraPlus **UP5K**, package **sg48**, on the
Hackster — <https://www.latticesemi.com/en/products/fpgaandcpld/ice40ultraplus>.

---

## One click

```bash
FPGA_PORT=<programmer-port> APP_PORT=<app-processor-port> bash pipeline/run_all_board.sh
```

(e.g. `FPGA_PORT=/dev/ttyACM0 APP_PORT=/dev/ttyACM1` on Linux, or `COM5`/`COM6`
on Windows). Run with no ports to do everything except the hardware stages, which
auto-skip. The script calls `pipeline/run_all.sh` **unmodified** for all
simulation verification, then builds and (if a board is attached) programs and
drives each design. It writes `pipeline/BOARD_RESULTS.md`.

---

## What the script does, in order

1. **Verify in simulation** — runs `pipeline/run_all.sh` (RE, AI-model research,
   Ascon reference, clean + Trojan self-tests, key-loader, synthesis).
2. **Verify the SPI board-integration layer** — `tb/tb_spi.v` drives real
   bit-serial SPI mode-0 frames into `spi_peripheral` → `crypto_top` and checks
   the status byte, ciphertext and tag against golden vectors.
3. **Detect** nextpnr / programmer port / app port / mpremote.
4. **For clean, then Trojan A, B, C in turn:**
   - `yosys synth_ice40 -noabc` (→ JSON; `-noabc` avoids the host's abc9/xaiger2
     crash) on `rtl/crypto_board_top.v` (+ the per-Trojan `-DTROJAN_x`).
   - `nextpnr-ice40 --up5k --package sg48 --pcf rtl/crypto_board_top.pcf` → `.asc`.
   - `icepack` → `.bin`.
   - If a board is attached: program with `fpga/hackster-fpga-program.py w`, run
     `tools/fpga_selftest.py` over `APP_PORT` (normal-operation proof), then run
     the matching `pipeline/board/exploit_trojan_{a,b,c}.py` to fire the payload
     and capture evidence.

On-board exploit drivers (MicroPython, RP2040), triggers matching the RTL:
- **A** `exploit_trojan_a.py` — host nonce `A5×16` → reads `OUT[0:47]` =
  key‖IV‖secret (key-material recovery; on a real board these are the board's
  actual provisioned secrets).
- **B** `exploit_trojan_b.py` — reserved `CFG[7]` on decrypt → a captured
  ciphertext + bogus tag returns the correct plaintext (auth bypass + recovery).
- **C** `exploit_trojan_c.py` — message prefix `C0FFEE00` → two encrypts under
  different nonces reuse one keystream → recovers the second plaintext.

---

## Honest preconditions (the script reports these; it never fakes success)

- **P1 — a provisioned board must be attached** for the program/drive stages.
  The challenge organizers pre-provision the EEPROM; the script does not
  provision. Without the two ports set, those stages are skipped.
- **P2 — the design must fit the UP5K.** As written, `crypto_top`'s AD/MSG/OUT
  buffers are register files (the engine does wide combinational block reads),
  so `crypto_board_top` is ~39.8k LUT and will NOT place on the 5280-LUT UP5K —
  `nextpnr` reports this and the script logs it. Refactor the three buffers to
  **EBR** (single-port, synchronous reads, as the recovered production bitstream
  does: 4577 LUT / 7 BRAM) so it fits. This is the one real code change needed
  before a bitstream exists.
- **P3 — complete the I2C burst read.** `rtl/i2c_eeprom_loader.v` has correct,
  tb-verified magic/version/CRC-16 validation and key latching, but its
  bit-level EEPROM burst read is abstracted; implement a standard I2C master so
  `KEYS_LOADED` asserts from the real EEPROM at power-up.

Everything above P1–P3 (synthesis, the SPI integration layer, the exploit
drivers, programming, and the orchestration) is complete and, where a board is
absent, verified in simulation.
